name: Invalidation

subjectOf.text: Shareholder agreement terms that limit board authority are vulnerable to invalidation, and the dominant judicial rationale is that such agreements tie the hands of directors and make it impossible for them to exercise discretion over the matters the agreement settles.
subjectOf.abstract: Courts offer varying rationales for nullifying terms of shareholder agreements that limit the board's authority, but most often, courts worry the agreements "tie the hands of the directors," making it impossible for them to exercise their discretion concerning matters decided in the agreement.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Shareholder Agreements - National Report of the United States of America (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3017612
scope_conditions: provisions that encroach on the directors' statutory authority to manage the business and affairs of the corporation

subjectOf.text: Delaware fiduciary standards create litigation exposure for LER: if distributions are judged disproportionate under Unocal or Blasius, boards face court invalidation and roughly $1 to $3 million in cost per dispute.
subjectOf.abstract: Delaware fiduciary standards, including Unocal and Blasius, add litigation risks if distributions are deemed disproportionate, potentially leading to court invalidations and associated costs of $1–3 million per dispute.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards in Corporate America (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5583610
